title: code-check keeps a renamed module on the mypy list
why: From banchi #993's review (c127), Oct 28 09:53 CDT (orchestrator): a module on a repo's mypy_modules list can drop out unnoticed when its file is renamed, and the shrink check compares against the PR's base commit, not current main.
note: Checked at main c71b22ef: actions/code-check/code_check.py lets a module leave mypy_modules once its file is gone (shrink check, line 100), and fails a listed path that is not a tracked file (line 205). So a rename that also removes the old entry passes, and the new path is never strict-checked. Next cloud lane: when git sees a listed module renamed since --base, require the new path on the list; and run the shrink check against current main as well as the PR's base. Red first on a fixture repo that renames a listed module and drops its entry. Touches actions/code-check/ only. Needs no answer. Port: yes, every repo that runs code-check (repos re-pin at their next code-check bump). Placed after c139 (triage 11, Oct 28): optional review finding, likely in normal work, since lanes rename modules. Green and reviewed (builder Opus; round 1 Opus, changes; round 2 Sonnet approve): draft PR #777, head 49a306ca. Waits on item 45 to merge.
